body.p: Evenki people seemed to dance the whole day until night fell. There was one old woman. She heard the noise of Korendo. "Boys, stop dancing when it has become night, terrible, some noise is heard." The children said "liar", they stuffed dog excrement into the deceiver's mouth. The Evenks did not believe the granny. Korendo came, it swallowed the Evenki dancers. The old woman covered [herself] up with her kettle, she stayed back alone. She lived, out of boredom(?) she thought to go through the forest. She left for the forest, she saw black grouse; where they had flown, there are excrements. She took the black grouses' excrements and brought them home. She put [it] into a cradle, she started to rock [it], she rocked and rocked [it], the black grouse's excrements fell apart. The old woman lived until it became spring. In spring the geese came. The old woman went to the river bank, she scared the geese. Where she scared [them], she found excrements, she took them, brought them home, put them into the cradle and started to rock it. She rocked and rocked it, the goose excrements started to peep. When it [DCh]: The started to peep, she rocked [it] stronger, on the third day it started to walk. analysis of the suffix "-lVkaËn" is tentative. When it had started to walk, it went to hunt Korendo. It found a small bird and brought it to the granny: "Granny, is it this one who ate my elder brothers?" [The granny said:] "Boy, no, that's an animal of God, bring it back, where it was, let it [free] there." Unyany brought [it] there, where he had caught it, and let it [free]. He caught a hazel grouse and brought it to the granny: "Granny, is it this one who ate my elder brothers?" â "Boy, no, that's an animal of God, let it [free], where it was." Unyany brought it there, where he had caught it, [then] he caught a black grouse and brought it to his mother. "Granny, is it this one who ate my elder brothers?" â "Boy, no, that's an animal of God." He brought it back, he caught a wood grouse. Then he brought all animals to his grandmother, he brought a wild reindeer, an elk, then he brought a bear. All of them, the grandmother made him to bring them back. The grandmother said: "That's an animal of God, it didn't eat your elder brothers, it went up." Unyany started to forge wings. He forged, he became able to fly, he asked his grandmother: "Where is Korendo, did he fly at [the height of a black grouse]?" â "Boy, [he flew] higher." Unyany made his wings bigger, he flew up again, he asked: "Where did Korendo [fly to], did he fly at [the height of a black grouse]?" â "No, a bit higher." He made his wings bigger again, he flew higher than Korendo's flight(?). The grandmother said: "Boy, Korendo flew lower." Unyany flew along Korendo's trace. He arrived at Korendo's wife. Unyany sang: "Scraper, Scraper, Little Scraper, from Korendo to his landing, [is it] far to his landing, from Korendo to his landing?" Scraper [name of the woman] said: "Eh, you, such one, you're competing(?), who you are (?)." Unyany landed, he destroyed(?) the placed where Korendo landed. He flew up again, he reached another woman, Scraper. "Scraper, Scraper, Little Scraper! From Korendo to his landing, [is it] far to his landing, from Korendo to his landing?" "Eh, you, such one, you're competing(?), who you are (?)." Unyany flew to the third woman(?), to Fullery. "Fullery, Fullery, Little Fullery! From Korendo to his landing, [is it] far to his landing, from Korendo to his landing?" "Eh, you, such one, you're competing(?), who you are (?)." Unyani flew on to the fourth wandering [descriptive name of women], [to] Pincushion. "Pinchushion, Pincushion, Little Pincushion! From Korendo to his landing, [is it] far to his landing?" "Eh, you, such one, you're competing(?), who you are (?)." Unyany flew to Grindstone. "Grindstone, Grindstone, Little Grindstone! From Korendo to his landing, [is it] far to his landing?" "Eh, you, such one, you're competing(?), who you are (?)." Unyany fly to Iron Scraper, then to Needlecase. Unyany reached Korendo. Korendo had eaten the Evenks. Unyany started to sing: "Korendo, Korendo, Korendo, Korendo, let's compete [with] our wings(?)! Over the middle of mother Sea, with our wings(?)." "Unyany, Unyany, Unyany! Don't, don't! I'll eat, I'll eat!" "Why will you eat? I take revenge for the elder brothers and sisters." The Evenks came out of his belly, part of them alive, part of them dead. Unyany started to [compete] in singing with Firstborn Korendo. "Firstborn Korendo, let's compete with our wings at the middle of Mother Sea." "Unyany, Unyany, don't. Don't, don't. I'll eat, I'll eat!" "Firstborn Korendo, why will you eat? Unyany cut off his [=Korendo's] belly with his wing. The Evenks came out of his belly, partly alive, partly dead. So Unyany sang and flew with two more children of Korendo, so he tore their bellies and freed the Evenks. Then Unyany flew to(?) Korendo's women. He started to sing: "Grindstone, Grindstone, Little Grindstone! We killed your Korendo, (the one who had swallowed many people), over the middle of the sea."
